hero.h1: Tree pruning, removal and vegetation management in Greater Victoria
hero.lede: Pruning, removals, invasive plant control and brush clearing, with a check of your municipality's tree bylaw before any cut. Garry oak and arbutus are protected at small sizes in many places.

audiences.body: Overgrown hedges, crowded trees or a yard taken over by ivy and blackberry, handled with the right permits checked first.

audiences.title: Stratas and property managers

includes.title: Invasive plant control
includes.body: English ivy, Himalayan blackberry, Scotch broom, laurel and other invasives removed and disposed of to CRD guidance.

includes.title: Brush and lot clearing

localRules.heading: Local rules that affect tree work
localRules.intro: Tree bylaws differ across the 13 municipalities. These examples show why we check the bylaw for your address before any cut.

items.text: Saanich: a tree cutting permit is required before cutting a protected tree, even if dead or dying. Garry oak, arbutus, Pacific dogwood and Pacific yew are protected at 2 m tall or 4 cm diameter.
North Saanich: topping is prohibited, a permit is needed to remove a regulated tree, and the permit must be posted 48 hours before work.
Colwood: removal needs a Tree Management Permit; pruning within stated limits (keep at least 50% live crown, no more than 25% removed per season) does not.
CRD: invasive plants must be disposed of properly, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

localRules.areasLink: Find the tree bylaw for your municipality on our [service area pages](/areas/).

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to remove a tree?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Each municipality in Greater Victoria has its own rules, and protected species like Garry oak and arbutus are covered at small sizes in many places. We check before any work. See our [area pages](/areas/) for local links.

faqs.q: Will you apply for the permit?
faqs.a: We can help you prepare the information the municipality asks for. The permit decision is the municipality's.
No. Topping harms trees, and [North Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw](https://www.northsaanich.ca/node/51) prohibits it.

faqs.q: Can a dead tree be removed without a permit?
faqs.a: Not always. Under [Saanich's Tree Protection Bylaw](https://saanich.ca/EN/main/community/natural-environment/trees/tree-protection-bylaw.html), for example, a tree cutting permit is required before cutting a protected tree even if it is dead or dying. We check the bylaw for your address first.

faqs.q: When can you do work near nests?
faqs.a: We plan around nesting season and check for active nests before work. Several bylaws, including [Saanich's](https://saanich.ca/EN/main/community/natural-environment/trees/tree-protection-bylaw.html) and [View Royal's](https://viewroyal.ca/EN/main/discover/environment/tree-protection/tree-protection-bylaw.html), also protect trees with certain nests.
